meaning: Aristotle's retorsion (Physics VIII.3, 254a27-30): the Eleatic thesis that nothing is moved is refuted by its being held, since opining is a motion. Refutes STMT-ELEATIC-NOTHING-IS-MOVED given its open premises, above all STMT-OPINION-IS-A-MOTION. No refutes relation is recorded until its premises are closed (#391). It does not refute McTaggart's rival STMT-CHANGE-UNREAL-BUT-APPEARS, which denies exactly that premise for appearances, and its conclusion is the double negation that it is not the case that nothing is moved (¬∀¬), reached through a motion in the respect of an opinion; it does not show that anything is moved in the world of sense. The Comparator config also verifies needsOpinionIsMotion and needsThesisHeld: each premise is needed.
